Miscellaneous: Semiplatmated plover occurs as migrant only.
Name: Snipe, Sandpiper - Family Scolopacidae (partial)
Montana resident in: Spring, summer, fall.
Habitat: Rangeland (curlew, plover) streamside, lake, shores, ponds, marshes, wet meadows. Most nest in small ground depressions of natural material (rock, tundra, leaves).
Foods: Insects, crustaceans, mollusks, worms.
Miscellaneous: Includes: long-billed curlew, upland plover, spotted solitary, Bairds, least, western and buff-breasted sand pipers, greater and lesser yellow legs, willet, sanderling.
Name: Snipe, Sandpiper - <u>Family Scolapacidae</u> (<u>partial</u>)
Montana resident in: Spring, summer, fall, migratory only.
Habitat: Marshes, ditches, streamsides, bogs, meadows, mudflats, prairie pools. Nests in shallow depressions on ground.
Foods: These birds feed on plants more than the above group. Insects, crustaceans, mollusks, worms, clover, sunflower, sedge, cattail, pondweed, bullrush.
Miscellaneous: Includes: common snipe, pectoral, white-nimped, semipalmated and stilt sandpipers, long-billed dowitcher and the markled and Hudsonian godwits.
Name: American Avocet - Recurvirostra americana
Montana resident in: Spring, summer, fall.
Habitat: Marshes, mudflats, alkaline lakes, ponds. Nest in depression in the ground.
Foods: Mostly animal; Insects, crustaceans, mollusks, worms, pondweed, bullrush, algae.
Name: Wilson's Phalarope - Steganopus tricolor
Montana resident in: Spring, summer fall.
Habitat: Shallow lakes, marshes, pools, shores, mudflats. Nest in grass-lined hollows in meadows.
Foods: Plankton, aquatic insects, water fleas, snails.
Miscellaneous: Distinguished from sandpipers by swimming rapidly in a tight circle while feeding.
Name: Gulls - Subfamily Larinae
Montana resident in: Spring, summer, fall.
Habitat: Lakes, farmlands, cities, piers, refuge dumps, rivers, marshes.

Nest in colonies (usually) on ground (isolated areas).
Foods: Garbage, fish, mollusks, bird eggs, insects, algae, pondweed, gooseberry, wheat, oats, duckweed.
Miscellaneous: Beneficial birds through their scavaging and insectivorous food habits.
